findings.title: runSplitQuery re-interpolates already interpolated shard-split queries
findings.body: runSplitQuery now unconditionally applies datasource.applyTemplateVariables to every target. It is also called from shardQuerySplitting.ts after runShardSplitQuery has already applied template variables and after interpolateShardingSelector has rewritten the expression. This causes template replacement to run twice on the same query. Template replacement is not generally idempotent: dollar signs introduced by variable values or by the first interpolation can be treated as variables on the second pass, corrupting the LogQL expression or silently dropping text. It can also reapply variable/filter substitution multiple times. Consider an internal non-interpolating split path or a flag to skip interpolation when targets are already interpolated.

findings.title: $__range splitting guard is evaluated after interpolation
findings.body: querySupportsSplitting relies on isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr), and the comment says queries using $__range must not be split. Because the targets are now passed through applyTemplateVariables before this check, any $__range or ${__range} macro that is replaced will no longer be present in expr, so the query will be classified as splittable. This can split queries that were explicitly meant to be excluded and produce incorrect range vectors or results. The exclusion should be based on the raw query expression, or range macros must be preserved until after the check.

findings.title: Queries that interpolate to empty are no longer filtered out
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery filters query.expr before calling applyTemplateVariables, whereas the previous implementation interpolated first and then filtered. If a target has an expression such as a template variable that resolves to an empty string, it now passes the filter, is grouped/sharded, and can be sent to Loki as an empty query. The same missing post-interpolation filter exists in querySplitting.ts. Filter hidden/empty queries again after interpolation.

findings.title: Missing interpolation edge-case tests for $__range and empty results
findings.body: The new interpolation tests only cover $__auto and $step. They do not verify that queries containing $__range remain excluded from splitting after interpolation, nor that queries whose expression interpolates to an empty string are skipped. These are the edge cases made more fragile by moving interpolation to the start of the splitting pipeline.
